subject: physics
title: The eye and defects of vision
key_idea: The cornea and lens refract light to form a real, inverted image on the retina. Rods and cones detect it, and cone spacing sets how fine a detail can be resolved. Short sight, long sight and astigmatism are corrected with lenses of the right power.

sections.heading: The eye as a lens system

blocks.text: The eye is a refracting system that focuses light from an object onto the retina. The cornea and the lens together act as one converging lens.

items: The **cornea** does most of the bending of light, because light slows down a lot as it passes from air into it.
The **lens** adjusts the focus so that objects at different distances form a sharp image.
The image on the retina is **real** and **inverted**. The brain turns it the right way up.
The distance from lens to retina is fixed at about 17 mm, so the eye must change its focal length to see near and far objects.

items.meaning: The point where rays parallel to the principal axis meet after a converging lens.
The distance from the centre of the lens to the principal focus.
How strongly a lens bends light, measured in dioptres (D).
The eye changing the shape of its lens to focus on objects at different distances.

blocks.label: Lens equation
where: u = distance from object to lens (m)
v = distance from lens to image (m)

items: A converging lens has a positive focal length and positive power.
A diverging lens has a negative focal length and negative power.
Use real-is-positive: a real object or image has a positive distance, and a virtual image has a negative distance.
Powers of lenses placed close together add.
To see a **distant** object, the ciliary muscles relax and the lens is thin, so f is long.
To see a **near** object, the ciliary muscles contract and the lens is fat, so f is short.
The normal eye can focus from about 25 cm (the near point) to infinity (the far point).
The whole eye has a power of about 60 D.
The cornea and lens focus a real, inverted image on the retina.
Power in dioptres is 1 ÷ f, with f in metres.
The lens changes shape to focus on near and far objects.

blocks.text: The retina is the eye's photodetector. Its light-sensitive cells are rods and cones, and they decide how sensitive the eye is and how much detail it can resolve.

rows: Mostly away from the centre of the retina
Many rods share one nerve fibre
Each cone at the fovea has its own nerve fibre

items: The eye responds to wavelengths from about 400 nm (violet) to 700 nm (red).
Its sensitivity is not the same at every wavelength. The **spectral response** peaks near 555 nm in bright light, in the green-yellow.
The rods peak at a slightly shorter wavelength, near 500 nm.
The three types of cone respond most to red, green and blue light. The brain compares their signals to give colour.

items.text: Two points of light make two small images on the retina.
They can only be seen as separate if they fall on different cones.
There must also be a cone between them that is not stimulated, or they blur into one.
The smallest angle that can be resolved is about 1 minute of arc, roughly 3 × 10⁻⁴ rad.

items: The fovea has the best resolution, because its cones are very small and close together and each has its own nerve fibre.
Away from the fovea, rods share nerve fibres, so the brain cannot tell which rod was stimulated and resolution is poor.
That is why you look straight at the thing you want to see in detail.
Rods are sensitive but give poor resolution and no colour.
Cones give colour and good resolution in bright light.
Two points are resolved only if their images fall on different cones with an unstimulated cone between.

sections.heading: Defects of vision and correcting them

blocks.text: A defect of vision means the eye cannot form a sharp image on the retina. A lens placed in front of the eye changes the way light arrives so that the eye can focus it.

items.meaning: Short sight. Distant objects are blurred because the image forms in front of the retina.
Long sight. Near objects are blurred because the image would form behind the retina.
Blurring in one direction, because the cornea or lens is not equally curved in all directions.

items: The eyeball is too long, or the lens is too powerful, so the far point is closer than infinity.
A **diverging** lens spreads the rays slightly before they enter the eye.
The lens must make a distant object look as if it is at the far point of the eye.
So the image from the lens is virtual and at the far point. Its focal length is minus the far point distance.
The eyeball is too short, or the lens is too weak, so the near point is further than 25 cm.
A **converging** lens makes the rays converge slightly before they enter the eye.
The lens must make an object placed at 25 cm look as if it is at the near point of the eye.
So the image from the lens is virtual and at the near point.

items.text: For long sight, the object is at u = 0.25 m. The virtual image is at the near point, so v = −d.
P = 1 ÷ f, which is positive, so the lens is converging.
Use u = ∞ and v = −(far point). Then P = −1 ÷ far point, which is negative, so the lens is diverging.

diagram.alt: A practice question. Work out the power of the converging lens that corrects a long-sighted eye with a given near point.
diagram.question: A long-sighted eye has a near point of {d} m. Find the power of the lens that lets it see an object 0.25 m away clearly.
working: The object is at u = 0.25 m and the virtual image is at v = −{d} m.

items: The cornea is shaped more like a rugby ball than a football, so it has a different focal length in different directions.
Lines in one direction are in focus while lines at right angles are blurred.
It is corrected with a **cylindrical** lens, which is curved in one direction only.
A prescription gives the sphere power (D), the cylinder power (D) and the axis (an angle from 0° to 180°) of the cylinder.

blocks.text: For example, −1.50 / −0.75 × 90 means a sphere power of −1.50 D, a cylinder power of −0.75 D and an axis of 90°.

items: Short sight is corrected with a diverging lens, long sight with a converging lens.
Find the power with 1 ÷ u + 1 ÷ v = 1 ÷ f, putting the virtual image at the far or near point.
Astigmatism needs a cylindrical lens, written as sphere / cylinder × axis.

checks.q: State two reasons why the fovea has better resolution than the rest of the retina.
checks.a: It contains only cones, which are small and packed closely together. Each cone has its own nerve fibre, so the brain can tell which cone was stimulated.

checks.q: A short-sighted person has a far point of 2.0 m. Calculate the power of the lens that corrects their sight, and state its type.
checks.a: The lens must form a virtual image at 2.0 m of a distant object, so f = −2.0 m. P = 1 ÷ f = −0.50 D. It is a diverging lens.

checks.q: Explain, using a ray diagram idea, how a converging lens corrects hypermetropia.
checks.a: The eye cannot focus light from near objects because its lens is too weak or the eyeball too short. A converging lens makes the rays from a near object converge a little before entering the eye, so the eye can focus them on the retina. Rays appear to come from the near point.
